knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The load and the bent upright are not touched. Work below stops, people are kept out, and the site is told at once. Pushing the load back is a test the cleaner must not make.
Assessment, unloading, repair and re-stacking are decided by the site's authorised or competent person. A cleaner or any worker may stop work, but does not decide that racking is safe.
Torn bracing and bent uprights are damage signs named in the state racking guidance. A fresh coat of paint or a clean floor says nothing about the frame.

The WorkSafe Victoria and SafeWork NSW racking guidance both put formal competent-person inspections at intervals of no more than 12 months. The other two options are not what that guidance says. Checked 2026-11-03.

practicalCriteria: On a sample racking photograph, the worker names each warning sign present (bent or twisted upright, torn or bent brace, popped or missing beam or clip, leaning or overhanging load) with none missed.
On a simulated walkway below a marked damaged bay, the worker moves clear, closes the area with barriers or signs, does not touch the rack or stock, and does not restart work in the area.
The worker reports the simulated condition to the assessor acting as supervisor, giving aisle, bay, level, signs, time and who was told, on the report form.
passRule: Pass when all three practical criteria are observed and recorded by the assessor in a supervised desk or walkway exercise, with no stop-work criterion met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Annotated sample racking photograph showing the signs identified
Completed damage report form for the simulated bay
Assessor observation record for the walkway exercise
stopWorkCriteria: The cleaner touches, pushes, climbs or tests the racking or the stock
The cleaner re-stacks stock, straightens a beam or removes a damage tag
Work continues below a damaged bay in the exercise
completionRule: Practical sign-off by an assessor only. This assessment does not confer any licence, certificate or competence to inspect, repair or approve racking.
